site.title: Dr. Ibrahem Abboud | Anesthesiology, Neuroscience & Humanitarian Leadership
site.description: Anesthesiology & ICU resident, neuroscience researcher and co-founder of Ma'ak Association for supporting cancer patients. Latakia, Syria.

sections.kicker: Dr. Ibrahem Abboud · Anesthesiology & ICU Resident
sections.title: Medicine begins with *empathy*.
sections.lead: It is the most important quality I find in myself. It helps me feel for others, connect with them, break down barriers and build rapport, in the operating room, at the ICU bedside, in research and in the charity I co-founded.
sections.quote: "My sensitive nature comes from past personal experiences that make me care deeply about healing the suffering of others."

sections.title: Three pillars, one purpose
sections.subtitle: Clinical practice, academic research and science communication, held together by a commitment to humanitarian action.

blocks.text:
I am a medical graduate of Latakia University (formerly Tishreen University) and an anesthesiology resident. Daily work in the operating room and the neuro-ICU gives me a firsthand view of how anesthetic agents modulate central nervous system function and how patients with stroke or TBI recover consciousness.

That clinical view drives my research: molecular strategies to cross the blood-brain barrier, computational models of neural circuits, and better neuromonitoring (such as EEG) in resource-limited hospitals.

Alongside medicine, I co-founded a charity for cancer patients. It taught me that healthcare and humanitarian commitment are deeply intertwined, and that results are measured by what you achieve despite the constraints.

sections.title: Anesthesiology & Intensive Care
sections.subtitle: Resident at Latakia University Hospital (formerly Tishreen University Hospital) since March 2023.

items.title: Residency begins
items.text: Perioperative care for diverse surgical cases, with a focus on neuropharmacology and preoperative optimization for patients with neurological or psychiatric conditions.

items.title: Neuro-ICU & surgical ICU
items.text: Daily neurological assessment of neurocritical patients (stroke, TBI), managing delirium and sedation-related altered consciousness; supervising first-year residents and protocol adherence.

items.title: Emergency on-call
items.text: Multiple-trauma cases with neurological and vital assessment in the surgical emergency department.

items.title: Protocols & forms
items.text: Contributed to the pre-operative preparation form and hospital-specific protocols for surgical preparation.

items.title: Procedures & volume
items.text:
- 900+ surgeries assisted (general, spinal, sedation)
- 11 surgeries for critical neurological patients
- 30+ central venous catheters
- 70+ anesthetic lumbar punctures, plus diagnostic and therapeutic punctures

items.title: Teaching
items.text: Clinical anesthesia lessons for 4th-year medical students: drug effects, resuscitation, airway management and clinical cases; lectures to colleagues on advanced ICU topics.

items.title: Looking ahead
items.text: Advanced neuromonitoring such as EEG during surgery and in the ICU is still missing locally. I aim to turn my theoretical training in it into practice.

items.title: IgG fusion proteins for neurological disease
items.text: Narrative review on IgG fusion proteins as a blood-brain barrier-crossing platform for Alzheimer's and Parkinson's, with prospects for stroke and TBI. Focus on CD98hc, insulin and transferrin receptors. Presented orally during the ICGEB/AEC course.

items.title: Novel protein design for acute stroke
items.text: Collaborative design of a novel protein for acute stroke, tested in silico with computational analysis of its protein folding.

items.title: Global Neurotrauma Outcomes Study: Spine

items.title: Pediatric oncology records

sections.title: Ma'ak Association for Supporting Cancer Patients
sections.subtitle: From a student volunteer initiative in 2019 to a licensed NGO supporting cancer patients, orphans and disaster-affected families.

blocks.title: Co-founder & executive leader
blocks.text:
After our volunteer team "We Care" had to stop, I co-founded Ma'ak to keep children's cancer care alive. I handled the legal process across several governorates until we received our license (Ministry of Social Affairs and Labor, No. 2789, 22 Nov 2022).

I built the core departments from scratch (Medical, HR, Media, Finance), authored the annual strategic plans, and represented the association in health-sector coordination meetings with the WHO, while staying on the ground in psychosocial sessions with children.

items.title: "We Care" volunteer team
items.text: Started with fellow 4th-year medical students, covering the needs of children in the oncology building at Latakia University Hospital (1,000+ doses annually).

items.title: Chairman of the Board
items.text: Led the legal registration across governorates and the official launch of activities in December 2022.

items.title: Executive Director & Head of the Medical Program
items.text: Built the medical program structure, managed medical files and treatment services, oversaw ~20 department heads, and developed the 2024 and 2025 annual strategic plans.

items.title: Board Advisor & Strategic Planning Director
items.text: Authored the main developmental plan (60 worksheets), designed policies and procedures, and coordinated partners and donors.

items.title: Board Treasurer & Project Manager
items.text: Managing finances and project delivery across health, psychosocial, educational and relief sectors.

items.title: Support for Cancer Patients & Orphans
items.text: Medical treatment and diagnostics, psychological support events, and orphan support (education grants, food baskets, holiday clothing).

items.title: Dr. Hala Saeed's Charitable Project
items.tag: Latakia Governorate · Syria Trust · Souria Btjmana
items.text: Launched on 8 Feb 2023 after the earthquake, in memory of the doctors who lost their lives. Food, medicine, shelter and relief supplies, while still supporting cancer patients.

items.title: Supporting & Empowering Children with Cancer
items.text: Psychosocial and recreational support, educational support, and awareness sessions for the families of children with cancer.

items.title: Psychological Support Room Rehabilitation
items.text: Turned a gloomy hospital room into a safe, colorful activity space for children with cancer with a very small budget.

items.title: Educational Sessions Program
items.text: Closing learning gaps caused by long treatment, at the headquarters, in hospital or at home. Children who completed middle and high school certificates in 2024 were honored.

items.title: Medical Program
items.text: Free chemotherapy and diagnostics (PET, MRI, CT, tumor markers, histopathology with IHC, bone marrow and genetic testing) for pediatric and adult cancer patients.

items.title: Childhood Cancer Awareness Campaign
items.text: Global Childhood Cancer Awareness Month campaign covering eight schools and several children's activity centers, supported by a media campaign.

items.title: "You Are Stronger Than Cancer" Campaign
items.text: Launched at the Cancer Survivor Ceremony to highlight survivor stories and give hope and determination to current patients.

items.title: Coastal Disaster Relief
items.text: Relief aid for victims of multiple disasters in the Syrian coastal region, including necessities for the elderly and children.

items.title: Celebrations & Recreational Events
items.text: Christmas, Eid al-Fitr, Eid al-Adha and World Cancer Day events for children with cancer and orphans, with partner organizations, plus yoga and sports activities.

items.title: Community health activities
items.text: Regular blood donation campaigns (about 3 per year), medical points at public events, pharmaceutical support to medical points during the earthquake response, and infection-prevention awareness with the Syrian Arab Red Crescent.

items.title: Management & humanitarian training (UNDP CEP · WHO · UNICEF · GOPA-DERD)
items.text: Managing civil society organizations, financial and project management, Psychological First Aid, psychosocial support, parental care, life skills, initiative and disaster management.

blocks.title: My approach
blocks.text: What matters is not only the quantity of what I achieve but what I manage to accomplish despite difficulties. Whether resources are scarce or plentiful, I adapt to reality and invest everything available to multiply the result. In Ma'ak's first three years we worked with very limited funding and still reached thousands.
